response.sql: WITH g AS (SELECT p.SEX AS SEX, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM Laboratory l JOIN Patient p ON p.ID = l.ID WHERE p.SEX <> '' GROUP BY p.SEX) SELECT SEX, cnt AS test_count, cnt * 1.0 / (SELECT SUM(cnt) FROM g) AS fraction_of_total, cnt - (SELECT AVG(cnt * 1.0) FROM g) AS above_average FROM g WHERE cnt > (SELECT AVG(cnt * 1.0) FROM g)

assumptions.assumption: Patients with NULL SEX are excluded along with empty-string SEX, since the comparison SEX <> '' is not true for NULL; the request only mentions excluding empty strings.
The per-group average is the mean of the group counts (total records / number of sex groups) after the join and the empty-sex filter.

alternatives.interpretation: Keep patients with NULL SEX as their own group, excluding only empty-string SEX.
alternatives.sql: WITH g AS (SELECT p.SEX AS SEX, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM Laboratory l JOIN Patient p ON p.ID = l.ID WHERE p.SEX IS NULL OR p.SEX <> '' GROUP BY p.SEX) SELECT SEX, cnt AS test_count, cnt * 1.0 / (SELECT SUM(cnt) FROM g) AS fraction_of_total, cnt - (SELECT AVG(cnt * 1.0) FROM g) AS above_average FROM g WHERE cnt > (SELECT AVG(cnt * 1.0) FROM g)
